title: Transparent Internship Scheduling Tool with LLM-Integrated Explainability: A Comparative Analysis of MILP and the Heuristic Regret Approach
content: Healthcare schools must place students in a limited number of internship wards. Manual planning is slow and may be difficult to inspect or explain, and internship assignment must satisfy department rotation, institution uniqueness, ward capacity, internship round, and student preference rules. This study compares a capacity-constrained regret heuristic with mixed-integer linear programming (MILP). The heuristic builds assignments from the options available at each decision. The MILP reduces the total weighted cost for the full cohort. Both methods were implemented in JavaScript within a standalone browser application. Method-specific records were also exported for a separate large language model explanation step. The evaluation used 133 students, three internship departments, and 101 healthcare institutions in Austria. Each method produced 399 valid placements. The MILP reduced the total weighted cost by 3.5% compared with the heuristic, while the heuristic was about 106 times faster in the recorded run. In one anonymized explanation case, both explanations passed four constraint checks and cited evidence from their source records. The heuristic explanation received higher scores for alternative coverage, uncertainty, and depth. The results show a trade-off between cohort cost, runtime, and the detail available for explaining an individual assignment.
